name: PHANTOM QUORUM
description: A 2–6 player political intrigue card game played with a 108-card smart-ink deck in which card text, faction allegiances, and point values physically shift between rounds based on a shared table-reader device tracking play history — cards literally rewrite themselves to reflect the current political landscape of the game. The shifting text is visible to all players simultaneously, creating moments of collective shock when a key card's loyalty flips mid-round.
story_hooks: A Phantom Quorum deck begins shifting to display real classified corponation documents instead of game text — someone used the smart-ink platform as a dead-drop.
A player realizes the shifting card outcomes in their regular game group have been accurately predicting real district political events three weeks in advance.
The original programmer of the smart-ink shift algorithm wants it destroyed — and is willing to pay significantly for someone to find and burn every table-reader device.
